scientific_queries.note: Cross-screen replication with an attribution baseline on the locally held GDSC screen; no novelty claim.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the noise asymmetry between the two arms is disclosed in the record and report, and the conclusion is stated as 'no evidence of extra screen decay' rather than 'cross-screen is better'.

design.baseline: within the original screen every (cell, combination) has two anchor concentrations; agreement between those two isolates the concentration effect (n=107,714)
design.cross_screen: original mean vs validation mean on the 4,725 overlapping (cell, combination)
design.why: comparing screens directly would bundle a concentration change with a screen change

interpretation: the cross-screen correlation is at least as large as the within-screen concentration-change correlation, so there is no evidence of screen-level decay beyond concentration. The ratio above 1 is partly a noise asymmetry: the baseline values are single concentrations while the cross-screen values are means of two.
selection_caveat: the validation screen covers only 4,725 of 108,259 keys (4.4%) and is very likely a selected subset, which would inflate agreement; 0.689 is therefore an upper-style estimate

register_updates.F9: new fact: validation screen coverage and its likely selection
register_updates.C26: new, exploratory: cross-screen replication r 0.689 with no extra screen decay

next_gates: random-subset control inside the original screen at the same n, to test whether the validation subset was cherry-picked
